lines.text: GitHub rebuilt how it stores code, so thousands of AI agents can push at once.
Agents work in parallel and around the clock, so one repository gets far busier than before.
lines.title: Busy repositories

lines.text: Code files live in cheap blob storage. A small service called Ref-CAS tracks which branch points where.
lines.title: Two homes for data

lines.text: A push uploads its pack first. Then one small transaction updates the branch pointer.
lines.title: How a push works

lines.text: Ref-CAS only locks the branches being changed, so agents on different branches don't wait for each other.
lines.title: Little coordination

lines.text: Background workers merge many small packs into fewer big ones, so the servers answering requests stay fast.
lines.title: Compaction

lines.text: In tests, 5,000 agents sent 7,200 pushes per second to one repository, while reads stayed fast.
lines.title: Test results

lines.text: Git works the same for you. Underneath, only the branch pointer needs agreement, so everything else can scale.
lines.title: Takeaways
